title: Incremental tool-call consistency and local emulator spec
content:
Purpose
This is a working PRD sketch to define a compact set of semantics and SDK ergonomics for: (1) deterministic handling of interleaved tool calls during streaming responses, (2) a local emulator that lets developers run and debug tool-call flows without a live networked tool, and (3) a minimal structured-output binding that survives partial / incremental responses. Goal is to reduce developer friction when integrating complex tool chains and to make end-to-end behavior reproducible during development.

Context and motivation
- We see customers using the hosted streaming API to deliver long-running assistant sessions that call external tools (search, DB writes, HTTP actions). Current model surface (token stream + ad-hoc tool tags) leads to brittle client reconcilers and flaky replay tests.
- Debugging tool-call ordering, retries, and partial results is hard without a way to emulate server-side streaming and tool handshakes locally.
- Structured outputs that are assembled across partial responses get corrupted by mid-stream re-rolls / model fallbacks. We need a lightweight set of guarantees plus a local SDK pattern that encourages idempotent tool designs.

Non-goals
- This doc does NOT attempt to fully replace the existing typed-frame protocol proposals. It aims to sit atop the streaming channel and provide a pragmatic compatibility shim for SDKs and clients.
- Not trying to spec exhaustive schema languages; we support a tiny binding mechanism to track boolean checkpoints and JSON fragments.

User stories
- As a frontend engineer I want a deterministic playback of a streaming session (including tool call events) so I can build robust replay/debug UIs.
- As an ML engineer I want observable checkpoints that mark points where the model intends to call or has called a tool so I can metricize tool-usage quality.
- As an SDK author I want a single local emulator binary that can (a) simulate server streaming with controllable latencies and model fallbacks, (b) provide hook points for injecting deterministic tool responses, (c) surface the same events the real hosted API will emit.

Constraints
- Backwards compatibility: clients that ignore the new fields must continue to work: streaming text must still arrive as before.
- Thin-client friendliness: minimal handshakes so mobile/edge SDKs can implement cheaply.
- Security: emulator must never ship with production-only credentials; handshake tokens should be distinguishable as "dev-mode" tokens.

Key concepts and primitives
- Step token (step_id): a short stable token attached to a logical model step. Steps are the unit for tool-call coordination and partial-structured-output checkpointing.
- Event frames: the streaming channel will include compact event frames (text_chunk | tool_call | checkpoint | meta) serialized as JSON lines with a small prefix so existing stream-readers can skip unknown frames.
- Idempotency token: each tool_call frame includes an idempotency token generated by SDK or server; servers must surface repeated tool_call attempts with the same token so clients can dedupe.
- Local emulator: a CLI + Node/Python library that (1) accepts a sample config describing model behaviour (when to emit tool_call frames, what partial JSON fragments to emit), (2) exposes a dev-only endpoint that mimics hosted streaming SSE/WS frames, (3) supports deterministic replay files.

Streaming wire sketch (human readable)
- Server sends: [prefix][json-linelike-event]
- Example events in order:
  1) {"type":"meta","step_id":"s-13","model":"open-v2","seed":"dev:xyz"}
  2) {"type":"text_chunk","step_id":"s-13","text":"Looking up flights to SFO..."}
  3) {"type":"tool_call","step_id":"s-13","tool":"flight-search","idempotency":"id-993","args":{"from":"NYC","to":"SFO","date":"2025-10-03"}}
  4) {"type":"tool_result","step_id":"s-13","tool":"flight-search","idempotency":"id-993","result":{"offers":[... ]}}
  5) {"type":"checkpoint","step_id":"s-13","schema_path":"/itinerary","partial":{"destination":"SFO"}}
  6) {"type":"text_chunk","step_id":"s-14","text":"I found options, should I book one?"}

Compatibility notes
- Any client that only reads text_chunk events will see the same text as before. Clients that implement the event frames can rely on step_id to correlate events.
- Unrecognized event types should be ignored by default but logged by SDKs for developer visibility.

Structured output binding
- Minimal contract: a checkpoint frame contains schema_path (a dotted or slash path), and a partial JSON fragment. SDKs will assemble fragments into a final object and validate on final-checkpoint.
- Optimistic assembly: client assembles partial fragments as they arrive and exposes a "currentStructured" object to apps, with a confidence flag derived from whether partials were overwritten by a rollback/fallback.

Local SDK emulator: features and UX
- Modes: record (capture a live session to a replay file), replay (deterministic), scripted (feed a deterministic script), fuzz (introduce latency/packet loss).
- Hooks: dev authors can register tool shim callbacks that the emulator will call instead of reaching a live backend. This lets devs test payment flows, DB writes, or flaky external APIs without mocking infra.
- Session replay file format: line-delimited events with metadata, signed by the emulator to prevent accidental use in production tests. Small docs, human-editable.
- CLI example: redwood-emulator start --script ./tests/flight-booking.json --latency 120ms

SDK ergonomics recommendations
- High-level SDKs (JS/TS, Python): expose an AsyncIterable stream of events (events are union-typed strings), plus a lightweight convenience "onToolCall" callback that returns either a promise result or a pre-signed shim response.
- Default: SDK generates idempotency tokens for tool calls if app does not provide one. Provide an opt-in escape hatch so the app can supply its own idempotency token for cross-client dedupe.
- Client-side telemetry: capture timeline of step_ids, tool ids, and latencies. Provide helper to upload replay files to the console for customer support.

Operational and security considerations
- Emulator tokens: dev-only tokens should be rejected by production endpoints. Console should offer a single-button upload of replay files but enforce RBAC and retention limits.
- Observability: server should emit metrics for tool_call rate, tool latency distribution, fraction of sessions with unhandled tool_call frames. These should be exposed at route/model granularity.
- Resource isolation: hosted route that allows tool_call frames must opt-in per-account; default hosted routes continue to only emit text_chunk frames.

Migration and rollout plan
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement event frames on a dev flag for a single internal model; ship emulator alpha to platform-internal users. Collect feedback.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): extend SDKs to parse events; add replay upload feature in console; opt-in beta for selected customers.
- Phase 3 (quarterly): wider rollout, add advanced structured schema validations and enriched frames (confidence, token-level cost estimates).

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we standardize an extensible enum for common tool names (search, db-write, http-request) or leave tool naming completely free? (Action: product to decide)
- Should the emulator accept plugin binaries (e.g., npm packages) that implement tool shims? Security review required.
- What is the canonical replay file signing approach? HSM-backed signing for enterprise vs local signing for devs.

Appendix: quick API sketch for JS SDK (pseudocode)
- const stream = await client.stream({input})
- for await (const ev of stream.events()) {
-   if (ev.type === 'text_chunk') render(ev.text)
-   if (ev.type === 'tool_call') {
-     const result = await app.onToolCall(ev.tool, ev.args, {idempotency: ev.idempotency})
-     stream.respondTool(ev.step_id, ev.idempotency, result) // SDK helper to send result back to server if we own the tool
-   }
- }

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally small and pragmatic: it prioritizes developer productivity and debuggability over a large, rigid protocol. Feedback requested on the shape of event frames, the local emulator UX, and the rollout staging.
- Please add detailed comments inline in the doc and link to any product metrics or customer requests that would argue for/against alpha release in Q4.

-- end of draft --
